metadata.prompt: 请写一篇不少于1800字的中文技术说明，主题是“在个人电脑上构建分层专家缓存的混合 MoE 推理系统”。先用图书馆、流水线和操作系统内存三个准确类比建立心智模型，再依次解释路由、专家复用、GPU 常驻池、PCIe 搬运、CPU 直接执行、逐层调度、命中率与尾延迟。必须讨论静态热集、动态缓存、LRU、CLOCK、LFU、频率提升和成本感知混合策略各自的适用场景，并给出一个从单层到48层的端到端推演。全文使用连续、完整、信息密集的段落，包含公式化定义、反例、边界条件和最终决策表，不要提前结束。

metadata.prompt: Write a detailed English engineering essay of at least 1,800 words on designing a PC-scale hybrid Mixture-of-Experts inference runtime. Build a precise mental model, then explain token routing, expert locality, GPU residency, PCIe transfers, direct CPU execution, per-layer scheduling, tail latency, and the interaction between static hot sets and dynamic caches. Compare LRU, CLOCK, LFU, frequency-based admission, and a cost-aware hybrid policy. Include equations, a worked 48-layer example, counterexamples, operational boundaries, and a final decision table. Use complete dense paragraphs and continue until the requested scope is fully covered.

metadata.prompt: Design and explain a complete Python 3.12 implementation of an event-driven simulator for a 48-layer sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 512 experts per layer and top-10 routing. The simulator must accept a token-by-layer routing trace, model a byte-capacity GPU expert cache, and implement LRU, CLOCK, LFU, static-hot-plus-dynamic, frequency-gated admission, and cost-aware CPU-versus-H2D decisions. Provide type-annotated production-quality code, data structures, invariants, complexity analysis, deterministic tests, property tests, sample input/output, and a discussion of how to validate the simulator against measured hardware timings. Produce at least 1,500 words plus all necessary code, and do not abbreviate the tests or explanations.

metadata.prompt: Solve and thoroughly explain the following mathematical modeling problem. A decoder has 48 sequential layers. At each layer a token chooses 10 of 512 experts. Each expert occupies 2,764,800 bytes. A GPU cache has budget B in {2,4,6,8,10,12} decimal GB. Loading k missing experts costs a measured nonlinear function H(k), CPU execution costs C(k), and GPU-resident execution costs G(k). Formulate the optimal offline schedule, prove its relationship to weighted caching, identify why exact online optimality is unavailable without future routes, derive practical lower and upper bounds, then construct and analyze an online cost-aware policy that uses frequency and reuse distance. Include at least two theorems with proofs, one adversarial sequence, one stochastic model, numerical examples, pseudocode, and a sensitivity analysis. Make the answer at least 1,800 words and show every reasoning step.

metadata.prompt:
Read the following project note and then produce a self-contained architecture review of at least 1,600 words. Separate confirmed measurements, simulated results, projected results, and assumptions. Explain which conclusions transfer from a single routed layer to a 48-layer decoder and which do not.

PROJECT NOTE:
The workstation has a high-end desktop CPU, one consumer NVIDIA GPU, and a PCIe link between host memory and device memory. A sparse decoder contains 48 routed layers. Every routed layer selects 10 experts from 512 candidates. Each expert consists of three quantized affine matrices and occupies roughly 2.76 MB. The GPU has room for only a subset of all layer-expert pairs. Earlier isolated measurements established three useful execution modes: experts already resident on the GPU; experts copied from pinned host memory and then executed on the GPU; and experts executed directly on CPU workers while only the small activation and output cross the boundary. The transfer and CPU curves cross as the number of missing experts changes, so one global choice is inadequate. A prior synthetic cache study suggested that an aggregate cache near 8 GB could reach around sixty percent hit rate, but that study did not use real per-token router output. The present study therefore captures real top-10 IDs and normalized weights at every layer for several workloads, analyzes temporal and cross-workload locality, simulates several cache policies without future knowledge, validates a real mixed-path layer numerically, and measures whether GPU compute, host-to-device promotion, and CPU expert work overlap in time. The final design must make its decision independently at each layer and token, maintain a static hot region plus a dynamic region, and use measured costs and recent reuse as its inputs. It must not claim exact future-route prefetching.

Your review must reconstruct the information flow from token to router to cache lookup to per-expert execution to weighted merge. It must identify the dominant bottlenecks, explain the purpose of every validation gate, propose an experiment matrix, give acceptance criteria, and end with a decision among GPU-only, CPU-only, static partitioning, or a dynamic hybrid architecture. Continue until all requested sections are complete.
